title: Petra and the Ledger
premise: In the winter of 1917, Jude Dunmore keeps a secret ledger in a riverfront workshop, recording the names of wounded soldiers that officers strike from official reports. When the season's last bridge closes and the ice begins to groan on the river, she has until spring thaw to finish transcribing every name before the workshop is requisitioned and burned with its records. Torn between a duty-bound major who offers her safety across the river and Elias, the deserter-printer whose press made her ledger possible, she chooses to stay and finish the work — losing the bridge, nearly her life, and the man she loves, but carrying the names out over the ice herself as it breaks.
about_author: Coral Okonkwo is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing field hospital records from the Great War before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted print shop in Lisbon, where she still repairs letterpresses by hand.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In a flooded field hospital near the river town of Vellmere, Jude records in her ledger the names officers omit from casualty reports. Establishes her ritual, her guilt, and the workshop where Elias prints her pages. Emotional beat: quiet defiance born of grief.

chapters.title: Orders Come Down
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A requisition order announces the workshop will be seized at spring thaw; all unofficial records are to be destroyed. Jude hides the ledger inside a crate of type blocks. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Major's Offer
chapters.summary: Major Halloway's POV. Halloway, who once struck names himself, notices Jude's questions and offers her passage on the last convoy across the bridge — protection in exchange for silence. Beat: temptation dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: Elias at the Press
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The deserter-printer reveals he deserted after being ordered to print falsified rolls; his press is the only one that can duplicate the ledger before destruction. Beat: two keepers of secrets recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Bridge Closed for the Season
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ice floes force the closure of the only bridge; the convoy leaves without her. She watches Halloway cross and understands the offer has an expiry. Beat: abandonment hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: Inventory of What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She measures the world in what fits in a satchel: the ledger, ink, a photograph, ration tins. Elias argues the press must be saved too; they quarrel. Beat: love tested by priorities.

chapters.title: The First Name
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Jude's POV. Her brother Thomas's name was omitted from a report after a doomed advance; the ledger began with him. Beat: origin of the vow.

chapters.title: Winter Quarters
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The workshop becomes a refuge for two convalescents and a runaway orderly, straining food and secrecy. Jude teaches the orderly to set type. Beat: fragile community forming under threat.

chapters.title: Halloway Returns
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Stranded on the wrong side when the bridge closed, Halloway takes quarters nearby and resumes his offer — now laced with genuine feeling for Jude. Beat: the triangle tightens.

chapters.title: Copying by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Nightly transcription sessions; the press works but paper runs short. They salvage blank ledgers from a drowned supply depot. Beat: intimacy growing through shared labor.

chapters.title: The Orderly's Confession
chapters.summary: Orderly Bram's POV. Bram admits he informed on a printer in another town, dooming him. Trust in the workshop cracks. Beat: paranoia arrives with the cold.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A provost inspection sweeps the quarter; the ledger hides beneath a dying soldier's cot while Jude performs triage above it. Beat: terror held behind steady hands.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Halloway discovers the ledger's existence but says nothing — instead warning Jude that thaw patrols will burn the quarter regardless of orders. Beat: his conscience splits him open.

chapters.title: The Drowned Depot
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Retrieving paper, Elias falls through ice and is pulled out half-frozen; Jude nurses him through fever. Beat: love admitted aloud for the first time, in delirium and answer.

chapters.title: Names Without Bodies
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A mass of unidentified dead arrives; Jude refuses to let them go unnamed, interviewing the dying by candlelight. Beat: the ledger's purpose made flesh.

chapters.title: Bram Disappears
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Bram vanishes with a page of the ledger; the workshop fears betrayal. Jude insists on believing in him. Beat: faith versus evidence.

chapters.title: The Major's Ledger
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Revealed: Halloway kept his own list of men he erased, unable to forgive himself. He gives it to Jude to merge with hers. Beat: rival keeper becomes ally.

chapters.title: Thaw Patrols
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Word comes the burning will come early — within days of first break-up on the river. The deadline compresses. Beat: clock now audible in every scene.

chapters.title: The Press Must Break
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. To move the copies, the press must be dismantled; Elias grieves destroying his life's machine. Beat: sacrifice of identity for purpose.

chapters.title: Bram Returns
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram returns half-dead, having carried his stolen page to a chaplain who can smuggle copies south. Redemption offered, not yet accepted. Beat: forgiveness as choice.

chapters.title: Love Against the Crossing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Halloway finds one last crossing — a ferryman willing to run the ice for three passengers. He asks Jude to come; she asks Elias; Elias tells her to go. Beat: the choice laid bare.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Ferryman Osk's POV. Osk will take the ledgers but not the press parts; he has lost sons to unnamed graves and wants the names more than anything. Beat: strangers bound by the same grief.

chapters.title: Packing the Dead Men's Names
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The merged ledger — hers, Halloway's, the chaplain's page — is sealed in oilcloth and weighted to float. Rehearsal for the river. Beat: solemnity before storm.

chapters.title: First Crack
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Jude's POV. The river speaks in the night; ice groans like artillery. Everyone wakes. The burning detail is spotted on the far road. Beat: dread made sound.

chapters.title: The Chaplain's Gamble
chapters.summary: Chaplain Wren's POV. Wren departs south with half the copies, knowing capture means execution for carrying them. Farewell scene. Beat: hope sent ahead into danger.

chapters.title: What Halloway Cannot Carry
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Halloway realizes he cannot cross with Jude and remain the man trying to become better; he volunteers to draw off the patrol. Beat: duty transfigured into love.

chapters.title: The Burning Begins
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Smoke rises from the eastern quarter; the workshop is next. Final pages still drying. Elias works the press until the last sheet. Beat: race against fire.

chapters.title: Last Impression
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The final pull of the lever; Elias smashes the press rather than leave it for the army. He burns his own fingers doing it. Beat: grief and liberation in one act.

chapters.title: The Bridge That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They reach the bridge site — span collapsed by ice days early. No crossing exists. Beat: despair at the water's edge.

chapters.title: Osk's Ice Road
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. Osk knows a shelf of shore-fast ice that may hold a walker's weight until full break-up. It is a gamble measured in hours. Beat: terrible hope.

chapters.title: Choosing to Stay Behind
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias's frostbitten hands cannot grip; he cannot make the crossing and knows it. He gives Jude the type block stamped with Thomas's name. Beat: love choosing the other's survival.

chapters.title: Over the Ice
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The crossing itself — cracking sheets, black water, the ledger strapped to her chest, Halloway's voice counting her steps from the far bank. Beat: pure sustained terror.

chapters.title: Break-Up
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She reaches the far shore as the ice shelf disintegrates. The workshop burns behind her; Elias and Osk are seen on the near bank, alive, waving. Beat: relief braided with loss.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Chaplain Wren's POV. In a southern garrison church, the copied ledger is read aloud, name by name, families summoned by letter. Beat: catharsis; the work fulfilled.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Halloway submits himself to inquiry over the falsified rolls, using the ledger as evidence, ending his career deliberately. Beat: accountability chosen freely.

chapters.title: What Jude Carries Now
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Aftermath inventory: the original ledger, a broken type block, a pressed flower from Elias. She measures what survived against what didn't. Beat: mourning with gratitude.

chapters.title: Letters Across the River
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Correspondence with Elias resumes once the ferry runs again; his letters carry printed ornaments, small proofs he still makes things. Beat: love persisting at distance.

chapters.title: The Workshop Rises Again
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias rebuilds a smaller press in a free town; the first job is printing the ledger as a book so no family need depend on rumor. Beat: rebirth through craft.

chapters.title: Petra
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Years later, Jude visits the stone bridge rebuilt over the river — petra, the rock it's named for — and reads the published ledger's dedication: to those who carried the names. Beat: permanence won from impermanence.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude adds a final line to her personal copy — her own name, entered among the ones she saved — and closes the book. Beat: peace; the price paid and the inheritance kept.
